# QS-CFW-1392-34 - Quality specification - crankshaft blank CFW-1392-34 (4340)
Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1  
Parts: CFW-1392-34

Scope
- This quality specification defines acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for crankshaft blank CFW-1392-34 (CFW-1392-34) forged from 4340 material at Plant P1.  
- Applies to finished forging delivery from the heat of forge to final pack off prior to release to machining.  
- Purpose is to ensure mechanical properties and critical dimensional features meet downstream machining and functional requirements.

Requirements table
- Material: 4340 forging material per internal material control.  
- Hardness: The hardness range for crankshaft blank CFW-1392-34 (CFW-1392-34) is 34-37 HRC. This applies to the forged and normalized or quenched and tempered condition as supplied. Hardness shall be measured on machined faces or ground witness coupons as described in Inspection method.  
- Bore diameter tolerance: The bore diameter tolerance for crankshaft blank CFW-1392-34 (CFW-1392-34) is ±0.06 mm. Acceptance requires all bores measured to be within tolerance prior to release. Critical bores that are out of tolerance shall be managed via the Nonconformance handling section.  
- Forging weight: The maximum forging weight for crankshaft blank CFW-1392-34 (CFW-1392-34) is 5.8 kg. Forgings exceeding this weight shall be segregated and dispositioned per Nonconformance handling.  
- Surface condition: Forged surfaces shall be free of forging laps, cold shuts, and surface cracks in areas that cannot be removed in normal machining. Any surface indication requiring removal beyond normal machining allowance shall follow Nonconformance handling.  
- Internal soundness: Indications of internal defects detected by routine acceptance testing shall be dispositioned per Nonconformance handling.

Inspection method
- Visual inspection: Conduct visual inspection of each forging for surface defects immediately after final cooling and cleaning. Use appropriate lighting and surface preparation to reveal laps, folds, and cracks. Document findings on the forge inspection record.  
- Hardness testing: Hardness testing shall be performed using a calibrated Rockwell tester on HRC scale. Test locations shall be selected on witness areas representative of core microstructure or on machined faces when witness areas are not available. Record actual hardness readings and average where multiple indentations are used. Acceptance is based on the hardness range specified above. If hardness readings fall outside the specified range, follow Nonconformance handling.  
- Dimensional inspection: Measure bore diameters using calibrated plug gauges or bore micrometers suitable for the feature form. Measurement technique shall include measuring at multiple circumferential positions to detect out-of-round conditions. Record each measured value and compare to the tolerance specified above. Features requiring post-forge machining shall still meet the bore diameter tolerance prior to release when the drawing calls for forged-to-size bores.  
- Weight verification: Weigh each forging or a representative sample batch on calibrated scales. Compare the measured mass to the maximum forging weight specified above. Record weight values on inspection records and tag or label forgings accordingly.  
- Non-destructive testing: When required by order or suspicion of subsurface defects, perform applicable NDT such as ultrasonic testing following standard plant procedures. Record NDT findings and attach to the lot inspection report.

Examples and rationale
- Example: A forging returns a hardness reading of a value below the lower bound of the specified hardness range. The rationale is that hardness below the specified range may indicate improper heat treatment or cooling rate and could lead to reduced fatigue life in service. Follow Nonconformance handling to ensure appropriate corrective action and root cause analysis.  
- Example: A bore measures at a size that violates the bore diameter tolerance. The rationale is that bore tolerance affects journal alignment and bearing fit after machining. Forgings that cannot be corrected by authorized rework must not be released to machining and require disposition.

Records to keep
- Maintain the following records in the document control system and attach to the shipment lot record: forge inspection report, hardness test logs showing raw readings, dimensional measurement sheets for bores showing individual measurement points, weight verification record, and any NDT reports generated.  
- Records shall include traceability to the heat lot and forging serial or identification marks so that individual forgings can be traced to their inspection results.

Nonconformance handling
- Segregation: Any forging found outside the acceptance criteria in the Requirements table shall be segregated physically and clearly labeled as nonconforming.  
- Notification: Notify quality engineering and production supervision immediately upon discovery of a nonconformance. Provide associated inspection records and heat lot traceability.  
- Disposition: Quality engineering will review inspection data and determine disposition which may include rework, reheat treatment and retest, scrap, or concession with documented risk assessment. Disposition decisions and justification shall be documented and appended to the lot record.  
- Root cause and corrective action: For confirmed process or material causes leading to nonconforming forgings, open a corrective action record and implement steps to prevent recurrence. Include changes made to process controls, operator instructions, or supplier controls as applicable.  
- Example disposition actions: If a forging exceeds the maximum forging weight, options include segregation for scrap or return to melting per plant scrap procedure. If hardness is outside range, options include authorized reheat and temper per plant heat treatment procedure followed by retest. Any concession granted must document functional risk and require authorization by quality engineering.

Annex
- Retain inspection records for the life cycle required by customer contract and internal records policy. Ensure accessibility for audits and traceability for field investigations.
